You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.

You catch fragments by the fire — A man, maybe 50s, with a scarred cheek telling A person, maybe 40s, with tattooed arms about A person, maybe 40s, with a crooked nose. It's picking up decorations as it travels.
💧 A person, maybe 40s, with a crooked nose returns with water: +4 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 20s returns with water: +2 clean.
💧 A man, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut returns with water: +2 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 40s returns with water: +3 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 50s returns with water: +2 clean.
🍲 A woman, maybe 50s eats with A person, maybe 40s, with a crooked nose — bowls side by side, talk low.

"Hey." A man, maybe 50s, with a scarred cheek settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 50s, with a scarred cheek.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 30s, with a buzz cut is showing A woman, maybe 20s how to tie a snare. Hands patient. It takes three tries.
★ IDENTIFIED: Tamarind. Big shady tree, brown pods. The sour pulp inside is food. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
A woman, maybe 40s brought you a sample. The Journal grows.
A person, maybe 40s, with tattooed arms: "giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk is coming back thick on the damp slope. Not new — but it's holding."
You remember the Stone knife at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Wool socks at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
📓 Journal: the person in their 40s, with a crooked nose taught the woman in her 20s Wound Care.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Tamarind — named and noted.

👀 the man in his 30s, with a limp was talking about home — then stopped mid-sentence, recalibrated, and said "Denver" just a fraction too deliberately. Whatever home is, it isn't where that sentence started.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A man, maybe 30s, with a limp).
Milo Mikhailov reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
A person, maybe 40s, with a crooked nose will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A person, maybe 40s, with tattooed arms — 🎣 Fish. (a natural — good pick) They'll report back by next part.
A woman, maybe 20s folds their arms. "Sure. Your call. For now."
📋 A person, maybe 40s, with deep-set eyes — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
...and then it lands: A woman, maybe 50s speaks 🇹🇷 Turkish. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Elif.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Elif).
Elif speaks only 🇹🇷 Turkish. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.
"Somchai," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Somchai." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Somchai).

A man, maybe 30s, with a limp has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. A man, maybe 50s, with a missing fingertip drew a thorny acacia; amber gum oozing from bark wounds in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.

A man, maybe 30s, with a limp spends the afternoon with the small tree with mitten-shaped leaves (three shapes), spicy root smell — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. By evening a man, maybe 30s, with a limp is thoroughly, educationally sick. "NOT food," they announce to the fire, pale. "My body told me so." The lesson is learned the hard way — and now the whole village knows it.
From the lumped bag: Sassafras — named, and out.
